name: Pame Theatro
client: Theatre guide for Greece (a goWebgo project)
role: Design, development, Claude API integration, MCP setup
summary: A guide to shows, theatres and people in the performing arts, where an editor uploads a press release and the Claude API fills in the show's fields as structured JSON; nothing is saved until a person checks it and presses Save.
details: Press release import with the Claude API: the editor uploads a PDF, DOCX, TXT, an image, or pastes text, and the Messages API returns the show's fields (title, dates, weekly schedule, prices, credits, venue, genre, press quotes) in a fixed JSON schema using structured output.
Human-in-the-loop by design: the JSON only fills the form; an editor reviews it and saves it. The model also returns editor notes listing anything unclear or missing.
The prompt forbids guessing: anything not in the press release stays empty, so the model does not invent prices, times or dates.
Secrets handled safely: the API key is read from a constant in wp-config.php or an admin-only setting, and is only ever shown masked. A key test calls the models endpoint, which costs nothing.
Clear error handling for the API: invalid key, no access to the model, file too large, rate limits or no credit, and temporary overload, each with a message the editor understands.
The admin can choose the model (Claude Opus or Claude Sonnet, about half the cost). Calls go through the WordPress HTTP API because the server has no Composer for the official SDK.

Custom plugin with content types and relations for shows, theatres and people, a show programme, sponsorships, contact forms, consent, and a management panel at /admin/ with its own REST endpoints (pt/v1).
Also uses the WordPress AI plugin with an OpenAI provider for editorial helpers such as alt text, excerpts and summaries.

name: Apollon Chalandriou
summary: Club website with a match center and next-match countdown, plus My Apollon: a members area where each parent sees only their own children, and an admin panel for the club office.
details: Public site: news, teams, academy, standings, seasons, match programmes and a next-match countdown.
My Apollon members area with separate roles for parents, coaches, the club office and the board; each role sees only its part, and parents see only their own children.
Internal app modules: training sessions and attendance, fees with charges, payment tracking, PDF receipts and payment notifications, player evaluations, a coach panel, data import and export.
Modules that bring in match fixtures from the local football association (EPSA).
Privacy guard and per-role page access to protect members' data.
Built on WordPress with Elementor (Hello Elementor child theme); about 75 custom PHP modules written with Claude over MCP (Novamira) in a sandbox folder.
